title: Foundations: Serenades - The Complete Guide
summary: What Serenades is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Serenades songs: Serenades are songs sung to a beloved: under balconies, at weddings, on anniversaries. The tradition runs from Renaissance lute songs through mariachi to modern first-dance ballads.

History: The serenade (Italian serenata, evening music) was formalized in the 18th century. Mariachi serenatas, Schubert's Ständchen, and modern wedding ballads all serve the same ritual.

How the songs work: Serenades favors the keys of G, D, C, F. Common forms include Through-composed devotion, no irony allowed; Waltz-time for the first dance. Players should master classical-guitar arpeggios first, then trumpet or violin obligato (mariachi style). Guitar serenades in open keys.

title: Greensleeves - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Greensleeves, a public-domain Serenades standard.
body:
Greensleeves (Traditional English, 16th century (registered 1580). Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Alas, my love, you do me wrong,
To cast me off discourteously.
For I have loved you well and long,
Delighting in your company.

Chorus:
Greensleeves was all my joy,
Greensleeves was my delight,
Greensleeves was my heart of gold,
And who but my lady Greensleeves.

I have been ready at your hand,
To grant whatever you would crave;
I have both wagered life and land,
Your love and good-will for to have.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Serenades accompaniment in G using the 'Serenade I–V–vi–IV' pattern:
G | D | Em | C

Technique: classical-guitar arpeggios. Guitar serenades in open keys.
facts: Form: Through-composed devotion, no irony allowed
